The main takeaway from our work is that

, by combining threshold-lowered non-tailed differential pair with bulk driving of the input transistors, the design of a class-AB OTA with (input) common mode voltage set to ( $ V_{\mathrm {\bf DD}} + V_{\mathrm {SS}}$ )/2 can be achieved without the need of additional circuitry for bulk driving, and without any increase of the number of transistors.
, by exploiting a shared bulk terminal, a single CMOS OTA can be made to operate with a wide range of input common-mode voltages, including those close to ground.

a low-voltage CMOS OTA with a large input voltage swing can be designed without resorting to nonstandard devices and without sacrificing the dc gain and bandwidth, which are the most critical specifications of an operational amplifier for high-precision applications.
